findings.claim: S3StorageService.getDataWithMetadata takes the length from the multipart client's GetObject response, which is part 1's Content-Length, so any object stored in more than one part reports a fraction of its real size.
findings.failure_mode: If merged as-is, on S3 storage (multipart on by default) a complex obs over 8 MiB reports e.g. 8388608 instead of 20971520 as its length. legacyui's ComplexObsServlet sets Content-Length from ComplexData.getLength(), so downloads are silently truncated. CI cannot catch it because S3Mock ignores partNumber.
findings.evidence: AWS SDK 2.32.13 sources (bom awsSdkS3Version): DownloadObjectHelper.downloadObject splits the transformer and fetches by partNumber; SplittingTransformer forwards only the first onResponse upstream; MultipartDownloaderSubscriber itself adds response.contentLength() per part. Throwaway test against LocalStack 3.8.1 (local image) with 20 MiB multipart upload: HEAD len=20971520, GET partNumber=1 len=8388608 range='bytes 0-8388607/20971520' parts=3, getDataWithMetadata len=8388608 bytesRead=20971520, getMetadata len=20971520. Same test against S3Mock 4.5.0: partNumber ignored (full length, no range), so S3StorageServiceIT cannot see it. With the suggested fix applied, LocalStack gives getDataWithMetadata len=20971520 (small object still 1000). Suggestion confirmed spotless-clean via spotless:apply no-op, with a positive control (mangled spacing was restored). javap of legacyui-omod 3.0.0-SNAPSHOT ComplexObsServlet: ComplexData.getLength() -> setHeader("Content-Length").

findings.claim: LocalStorageService.read falls back to the legacy location only on NoSuchFileException, but a legacy key whose encoded name passes 255 bytes fails at the current location with FileSystemException 'File name too long', so the legacy file is never tried.
findings.failure_mode: If merged as-is, legacy (pre-2.8) complex obs whose title is long and non-ASCII (36+ Cyrillic or 24+ Amharic characters) stop loading once storageDir/<obs dir> exists, which it does as soon as any complex obs has been saved since 2.8. TextHandler/BinaryDataHandler throw APIException and ImageHandler returns no image, where master reads the file. This breaks the ticket's 'legacy-layout obs continue to load correctly' criterion.
findings.evidence: History: 80b4411f8^ AbstractHandler.getOutputFileToWrite names legacy files <title>_<uuid>.<ext>; BaseStorageService.encodeKey URL-encodes. Throwaway LocalStorageServiceTest probe with legacy file appdata/complex_obs/<n x U+0416>_<uuid>.txt and storageDir/complex_obs present: head n=10 reads, n=36 getData throws FileSystemException '...: File name too long' (exists() still true); master worktree (891b80745) same probe n=36 reads 'test'. Without storageDir/complex_obs present head also reads (ENOENT on the parent comes first). With the suggested read() applied, n=36 reads and the full LocalStorageServiceTest (incl. the PR's counting tests) passes. spotless:apply on the suggestion only removes the now-unused NoSuchFileException import, noted in the body. Linux check: Java 21 in a tomcat:11-jdk21-temurin container (Linux 5.15, overlay root) running Files.readAttributes on the encoded name with the parent directory present: 35 letters (253 bytes) throws NoSuchFileException, 36 letters (259 bytes) throws FileSystemException 'File name too long'.

findings.claim: The only call-count test drives AbstractHandler.getObs, which every bundled handler overrides, so the ticket's regression guard covers none of the handlers it is for.
findings.failure_mode: If merged as-is, putting a redundant exists() or separate getMetadata() call back into any of Image/Binary/BinaryStream/Text/Media handlers passes CI, so TRUNK-6682's 'unit tests assert the number of storage-service calls per getObs()' criterion is not met for any production read path.
findings.evidence: All five bundled handlers declare 'public Obs getObs(Obs obs, String view)' (grep). Mutation run: added storageService.exists(key) in BinaryStreamHandler and a separate getMetadata/injectMissingMetadata(key, cd) in Text/Image/Media/BinaryData handlers, plus the control mutation in AbstractHandler.getObs. Ran AbstractHandlerTest, TextHandlerTest, BinaryStreamHandlerTest, ImageHandlerTest, MediaHandlerTest, BinaryDataHandlerTest, LocalStorageServiceTest: only AbstractHandlerTest.getObs_shouldNotIssueRedundantStorageCallsForLocalStorage failed ('expected: <0> but was: <1>'); all handler tests green (5/9/5/4/5 runs). AbstractHandler.storageService/adminService are package-private fields, hence ReflectionTestUtils.

findings.claim: exists() dropped master's storage-dir containment check on the current-location path, so an absolute key outside storage reports true instead of throwing.
findings.evidence: master getPath (git show master:...LocalStorageService.java:88-101) asserts containment; throwaway probe on head: exists("/etc/passwd")=true; with the suggested two lines: throws IllegalArgumentException 'outside legacy storage dir' (master's behaviour), exists('/nonexistent')=false, full LocalStorageServiceTest passes; spotless:apply leaves it unchanged.

findings.claim: The obsDir null guard and its test fix a pre-existing master NPE unrelated to TRUNK-6682's I/O counts.
findings.evidence: Throwaway ImageHandlerTest probe on a master worktree (891b80745) with obs dir GP null and valueComplex 'jpg|2026/01-01/...jpg': NullPointerException 'Cannot invoke "String.isEmpty()" because "this.pattern" is null' from key.replaceFirst(getObsDir(), ...). The line is unconditional on the image being present.
findings.body: Could this guard and `getObs_shouldNotThrowWhenTheObsDirGlobalPropertyHasNoValue` go in their own ticket? Master throws the same NPE here for a bare-extension title whenever the obs dir property is unset, image present or not. That makes it a separate fix from the I/O counts, and leaving it out gives reviewers less to check here. Nothing breaks if it stays.

findings.claim: S3StorageService.getData duplicates getDataWithMetadata's GetObject call and 404 translation, so the two can drift.
findings.evidence: Read S3StorageService.java:129-156 at head: identical GetObjectRequest, toBlockingInputStream and translateNotFound; getDataWithMetadata(key).data() returns the same ResponseInputStream with no extra request.
findings.body:
This can just delegate to `getDataWithMetadata`, which repeats the same GetObject call and 404 translation (the duplication ibacher flagged in `LocalStorageService`, [comment](https://github.com/openmrs/openmrs-core/pull/6535#discussion_r3990739410)). The GET already carries the headers, so it costs nothing:

```suggestion
		return getDataWithMetadata(key).data();
```

verdict: Not ready to merge: on S3 storage, getDataWithMetadata reports part 1's size for any object over 8 MiB, so downloads through legacyui's ComplexObsServlet are silently truncated (also blocking: legacy long non-ASCII filenames stop loading, and the call-count test misses every bundled handler).
